The official roadmap states the Microsoft Teams integration is **under active design and planning, targeted for Q4 2026 (v2.11.0, November release)**, with a restricted pilot starting October 2026 for selected enterprise accounts; it is not generally available and the Slack connector is the only limited pilot currently available [NL-014#NL-014-S07]. Engineering confirms no active code is being written for Teams and that it is slated for design in Q4 2026 [NL-027#NL-027-S03].

Informal sales claims conflict sharply: a sales VP told a prospect the Teams integration was "basically right around the corner," "almost ready for general release," and could be included in a July pilot [NL-023#NL-023-S04]. Slack messages show sales pushing for a July/August pilot to close deals [NL-027#NL-027-S02]. Engineering and product staff describe the existing demo as a "toy" webhook with zero tenant isolation, zero permission mapping, zero SSO, and zero citation formatting, and they refuse to deploy it to production [NL-027#NL-027-S03]. The CTO and Product lead also confirm the OCR pipeline takes priority and that Teams remains in design for Q4, with development in early 2027 [NL-015#NL-015-S06]. The sales playbook itself instructs reps to consult the official roadmap and not guarantee launch dates, noting the Teams roadmap status is planning/design for Q4 2026 [NL-009#NL-009-S08]. Internal management also acknowledges sales overclaiming and is enforcing training to stop promising immediate Teams support [NL-016#NL-016-S05].

In short: official roadmap = Q4 2026 design/planning with October 2026 restricted pilot; informal sales/Slack claims = "nearly ready" with July/August pilot, which are contradicted by engineering, product, and the roadmap.
